label: thm:inverse
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:inverse}
(i) Let $Q\in C(I)$, let $\psi\in C^2(I)$ be a positive solution of $\ddot\psi=Q\psi$, let $\tau_*\in I$ be a point
at which $\int_\tau^{\tau_*}\psi^2\,\mathrm{d}\tau'$ is finite for all $\tau\in I$, and let $C\in\mathbb{R}$ be such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:inverse}
c(\tau)=\frac{C+\gamma g\int_\tau^{\tau_*}\psi^2\,\mathrm{d}\tau'}{\psi^2(\tau)}>0\quad(\tau\in I),\qquad z(\tau)=\int c\,\mathrm{d}\tau .
\end{equation}
Then $c\in C^2(I)$, $z$ is a strictly increasing map of $I$ onto an interval $J$, the potential (\ref{eq:KG}) of the
atmosphere $c(z)$ equals $Q$, and $w=u/\psi$ solves (\ref{eq:vert}) for every solution $u$ of (\ref{eq:KG}).

(ii) Conversely, for every atmosphere in the above sense with $c\in C^2$, the function
$\psi=\exp(-\frac12\int a\,\mathrm{d}\tau)$ is positive and satisfies $\ddot\psi=Q\psi$, and $c$ is given by (\ref{eq:inverse}) with this
$\psi$, any $\tau_*\in I$ and $C=c(\tau_*)\psi^2(\tau_*)$.

(iii) The overall scale of $\psi$ is immaterial, since the simultaneous transformation $\psi\mapsto A\psi$,
$C\mapsto A^2C$ leaves $c(\tau)$ unchanged. For a given $Q$, the admissible atmospheres are parametrised by the positive
solutions of $\ddot\psi=Q\psi$, modulo this scaling, together with the integration constant $C$.

title: Proof
body_md:
The gauge factor of \S\,\ref{sec:form} equals $1/\psi$ precisely when $a=-2\dot\psi/\psi$, and
then $\frac14a^2-\frac12\dot a=\ddot\psi/\psi=Q$. The relation $(\dot c+\gamma g)/c=-2\dot\psi/\psi$ is the linear equation
$(c\psi^2)\dot{}=-\gamma g\psi^2$, whose solutions are exactly (\ref{eq:inverse}); $c\in C^2$ because $\psi\in C^2$ and $\psi>0$, and
$z$ is strictly increasing because $c>0$. For (ii), $a=(\dot c+\gamma g)/c\in C^1(I)$, so $\psi\in C^2$, $\psi>0$, and
the same linear equation holds. Statement (iii) follows from (i), (ii) and the scaling invariance; positive solutions of
$\ddot\psi=Q\psi$, when they exist, form a convex cone in a two-dimensional space. \hfill$\square$
head: manual

title: Remark
body_md:
For constant $Q$, (\ref{eq:inverse}) gives in explicit parametric form the reflectionless profiles found implicitly
by \citet{PPT2012}: for $Q=0$, $\psi=1$ gives $c^2=C^2-2\gamma gz$, and $\psi=\tau$ with $C=0$ gives $c=-\gamma g\tau/3$,
$z=z_*-\gamma g\tau^2/6$, i.e.\ $c^2=\frac23\gamma g(z_*-z)$. The constant $C$ changes the atmosphere but not $Q$. A positive
zero-energy solution exists, for instance, whenever $Q\ge0$ (the solution with $\dot\psi(\tau_0)=0$ is then convex) and
for the Darboux--Crum potentials below, which covers all potentials used here.
